# The descriptive sweep — three size-distribution families, one axis each

*Generated by `sweep_descriptive.py` from shards already on disk. No new cells.*
*Every number below is printed by that script into `out/sweep_descriptive.txt`;
none of them is typed here by hand.*

## What was run

Three size-distribution families — lognormal, uniform, bidisperse — over CV 0.0–0.5, at matched friction `mu_p` = 0.3, N = 1500, on a four-rung reduced-pressure ladder. 252 converged cells survive the matched-condition filter; the counts before and after every filter are in the artifact.

## The result

The largest **resolved** across-family contrast is **contact force CV**, whose paired CV 0 → 0.5 change spans a factor **8.34×** between the three families (lognormal +0.3621±0.0078, uniform +0.1231±0.0114, bidisperse +0.0434±0.0133).

| observable | lognormal | uniform | bidisperse | across-family spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| phi_J | +0.0621±0.0026 | +0.0242±0.0008 | +0.0139±0.0025 | 4.47x |
| Z_all | -2.1769±0.0827 | -2.0000±0.0670 | -2.1938±0.0362 | 1.10x |
| Z_nr (k=2) | -0.1891±0.0284 | -0.0812±0.0162 | -0.1172±0.0393 | 2.33x |
| rattler fraction | +0.4082±0.0125 | +0.3827±0.0119 | +0.4171±0.0033 | 1.09x |
| contact force mean | +0.0009±0.0001 | +0.0011±0.0001 | +0.0012±0.0000 | 1.32x |
| contact force CV | +0.3621±0.0078 | +0.1231±0.0114 | +0.0434±0.0133 | 8.34x |

(CV 0 → 0.5 change, at `p_hat` = 1e-3 for the per-cell channels and extrapolated to `p_hat` → 0 for `phi_J`.)

### The ordering, which is the part worth carrying

Ranked by resolved across-family spread: **contact force CV** 8.34× > **phi_J** 4.47× > **Z_nr (k=2)** 2.33× > **contact force mean** 1.32× > **Z_all** 1.10× > **rattler fraction** 1.09×.

The two channels at the bottom of that list — `rattler fraction` (1.09×) and `Z_all` (1.10×) — are the **depopulation** channels, and they are very nearly family-independent: all three shapes strip the load-bearing network by the same amount across the CV ladder. What the shape of the distribution changes is `phi_J` and the **width of the contact-force distribution**, not how many grains fall out of the network. That is a partition of the effect, and it is read off the ordering above rather than assumed.

## What it does not say

- **The bidisperse column is a path, not a family.** It is 50:50 *by number*, so its fines carry 0.500 → 0.036 of the volume across this ladder: it never visits the composition where interstitial filling peaks. Matched binaries that differ only in which atom carries the volume pack 0.0635 apart.
- **A spread is not a pairwise separation.** These ratios say the families differ; they do not say two of them can be told apart at a given CV.
- **Only `phi_J` is extrapolated.** `Z`, the rattler fraction and the force moments are read *at* a pressure and move with the rung; the artifact prints all four rungs so the rung dependence is visible rather than chosen.

## Ladder health

`phi_J` is a four-rung extrapolation, and a 2026-09-13 review found an arm whose `phi_J` came from ladders that were 0/6 monotone. The same gate is applied here before any `phi_J` is quoted: **lognormal** passes, **uniform** passes, **bidisperse** passes.
